Maya Ortiz: Quick heads-up: opened a small docs PR to tidy Dedicated provisioning examples + SLA wording. It adds a short migration checklist, a compact autoscale YAML, and an SDK snippet showing tenant-label usage. PR: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/4999 Please review phrasing around evictions and the autoscale defaults.

Jared Liu: Skimmed. Two quick asks: 1) Replace 'best-effort' with clearer phrasing: 'not SLA-backed' for fallback tiers. 2) Call out scheduled maintenance as a possible preemption cause.

Hannah Park: On the autoscale YAML, include an explicit example labels block so customers know how to opt into tenant isolation. E.g.:
```
allocation:
  name: team-orbit
  labels:
    tenant_label: "team-orbit"
    isolation: "tenant"
```
Also bump cooldown default to 300s 999most teams see flapping at 60s.

Omar Idris: I tested a minimal Python snippet locally, feel free to paste under "Programmatic provisioning":
```python
from redwood import DedicatedClient
client = DedicatedClient(api_key="${REDWOOD_API_KEY}")
client.create_capacity(
    name="team-orbit-dedicated",
    region="us-west-2",
    scale_policy={"min_replicas":2, "max_replicas":8, "cooldown_seconds":300},
    labels={"tenant_label":"team-orbit","isolation":"tenant"}
)
```

Omar Idris: Small note to add under SLA: runtime may still preempt workloads for infrastructure maintenance or emergency mitigations; that behavior is not covered by the Dedicated latency SLA.

Maya Ortiz: Thanks 99I'll swap in Jared's phrasing, add Hannah's label example and the 300s cooldown, and paste Omar's SDK snippet. I'll also add a short smoke test checklist: 1) migrate a test tenant, 2) trigger multi-second traffic spike, 3) observe scale-up within expected window, 4) confirm cooldown prevents rapid scale-down, 5) verify label shows up in Console and observability dashboards.

docs-bot: Lint passed. Link-check found one outdated handbook anchor -> suggested replacement `#capacity-modes`.

Hannah Park: I'll push the anchor fix as a tiny commit.

Maya Ortiz: Perfect. Merging after CI and legal review of the SLA sentence.
